blocks.text: **The problem.** Implement a class `BSTIterator` over the in-order walk of a binary search tree: the constructor takes the `root`, `next()` returns the next smallest value, and `hasNext()` says whether any are left. The follow-up asks for `next()` and `hasNext()` in **O(1) amortized time** with **O(h) memory**.

blocks.alt: The tree 7, 3, 15, null, null, 9, 20. The iterator's stack starts with the left spine: 7, then 3 on top. next() pops 3. Then next() pops 7 and pushes the left spine of 7's right child: 15, then 9 on top. So the stack never holds more than one path from the root.

elements.text: keep only the left spine still to visit on a stack

blocks.code:
BSTIterator it = new BSTIterator([7, 3, 15, null, null, 9, 20])
it.next()     ->  3
it.next()     ->  7
it.hasNext()  ->  true
it.next()     ->  9
it.next()     ->  15
it.next()     ->  20
it.hasNext()  ->  false

blocks.text: Do the whole in-order walk up front into a list, then hand values out with an index.
**O(n) constructor, O(1) next and hasNext, O(n) memory.** Fast, but it fails the memory follow-up — and it does all the work even if the caller only wants the first value.
2. A stack of the left spine

Unroll the iterative in-order walk and pause it between values. The stack holds the nodes whose left side is done but which haven't been returned yet. `next()` pops the top (the smallest left), then pushes the left spine of its right child.

blocks.caption: next() pops the smallest pending node, then pushes the left spine of its right child.

blocks.text: **O(h) memory, O(1) amortized time.** One `next()` may push a long spine, but every node is pushed once and popped once over the whole iteration — n pushes spread over n calls.

blocks.alt: Flatten up front: O(1) per call time, O(n) space. Left-spine stack: O(1) amortized time, O(h) space.

items: **A single node** — one next(), then hasNext() is false.
**A chain going left** — the constructor pushes all n nodes; later calls push nothing.
**A chain going right** — the stack never holds more than one node.
**hasNext() called several times in a row** — it must not move the iterator.
**Reverse iterator (largest first)** — push the right spine and step into left children.
**BST Iterator II (prev and next)** — keep a list of returned values plus the stack.
**Two Sum IV in O(h) space** — one forward and one reverse iterator act as the two pointers.
**Peeking iterator** — remember the next value before it's asked for.
